Nihai Referans: Komut, Fonksiyon, Operatör, Veri Tipi ve Veri Yapısı Bu bölüm hızlı başvuru için yazılmıştır; fakat kuru liste değildir. Her aile önce görevine göre açıklanır, sonra sözdizimi ve örnekle bağlanır. uXBasic kitabında referans bölümü, okuyucuyu örneksiz bırakmamalıdır. ## 29.1. Temel giriş, çıkış ve değişken ailesi | Sözcük | Syntax | Görev | Kısa Örnek | |---|---|---|---| | `PRINT` | `PRINT ifade` | Ekrana veya hedef çıktıya değer yazar. `PRINT #` biçimi dosya kanalına yazar. | `PRINT "OK"` | | `DIM` | `DIM ad AS tip` | Değişken, dizi veya nesne alanı açar. | `DIM x AS I32 = 10` | | `AS` | `ad AS tip` | Değişkenin, parametrenin veya fonksiyon dönüşünün tipini bağlar. | `FUNCTION F() AS I32` | | `CONST` | `CONST ad AS tip = değer` | Program boyunca değişmeyen sabit tanımlar. | `CONST LIMIT AS I32 = 100` | | `REDIM` | `REDIM dizi(yeniBoyut)` | Dizi boyutunu yeniden kurar. | `REDIM veri(20)` | | `LET` | `LET ad = ifade` | Atamayı açık biçimde yazar; modern kullanımda doğrudan `ad = ifade` de kullanılır. | `LET x = 5` | | `INPUT` | `INPUT değişken` | Kullanıcıdan veya `INPUT #` ile dosyadan değer alır. | `INPUT yas` | Temel örnek: ```basic id="6ur8u5" CONST LIMIT AS I32 = 100 DIM okuma AS I32 = 76 IF okuma < LIMIT THEN PRINT "GUVENLI" ELSE PRINT "LIMIT_ASILDI" END IF ``` ## 29.2. Akış kontrol ailesi | Sözcük | Syntax | Görev | Birlikte Kullanılır | |---|---|---|---| | `IF` | `IF koşul THEN ... END IF` | Koşula göre program akışını kola ayırır. | `THEN`, `ELSEIF`, `ELSE` | | `ELSEIF` | `ELSEIF koşul THEN` | İlk koşul yanlışsa yeni koşul dener. | `IF`, `ELSE`, `END IF` | | `ELSE` | `ELSE` | Önceki koşulların hiçbiri doğru değilse çalışır. | `IF`, `ELSEIF` | | `SELECT` | `SELECT CASE ifade` | Tek ifadeyi birçok olası duruma göre ayırır. | `CASE`, `CASE ELSE` | | `CASE` | `CASE değer` | `SELECT` içinde eşleşme kolu açar. | `SELECT CASE` | | `FOR` | `FOR i = a TO b STEP s` | Sayaçla tekrar eden döngü kurar. | `TO`, `STEP`, `NEXT` | | `NEXT` | `NEXT i` | `FOR` döngüsünü ilerletir. | `FOR` | | `DO` | `DO ... LOOP` | Koşullu veya koşulsuz döngü bloğu açar. | `LOOP`, `WHILE`, `UNTIL` | | `WHILE` | `WHILE koşul` | Koşul doğru oldukça çalışır. | `WEND`, `DO` | | `UNTIL` | `LOOP UNTIL koşul` | Koşul doğru olana kadar döngüyü sürdürür. | `DO`, `LOOP` | | `EXIT` | `EXIT FOR`, `EXIT DO` | İçinde bulunulan döngü veya bloktan çıkar. | `FOR`, `DO`, `FUNCTION` | Akış kontrolü yalnız karar vermek değildir; veri işleme düzenini kurar: ```basic id="h8wyxe" DIM i AS I32 DIM toplam AS I32 = 0 FOR i = 1 TO 5 toplam = toplam + i NEXT i IF toplam == 15 THEN PRINT "TOPLAM_DOGRU" END IF ``` ## 29.3. Fonksiyon ve çağrı ailesi | Sözcük | Syntax | Görev | |---|---|---| | `FUNCTION` | `FUNCTION ad(parametreler) AS tip` | Değer döndüren adlandırılmış işlem bloğu kurar. | | `SUB` | `SUB ad(parametreler)` | Değer döndürmeyen işlem bloğu kurar. | | `RETURN` | `RETURN ifade` | Fonksiyondan değer döndürür veya bloktan çıkar. | | `DECLARE` | `DECLARE FUNCTION ...` | Dış veya önceden bildirilecek fonksiyon imzasını tanımlar. | | `CALL` | `CALL ad(...)`, `CALL(DLL,...)`, `CALL(API,...)` | Yerel, DLL veya API çağrı rotasını kullanır. | | `BYVAL` | `BYVAL x AS tip` | Parametreyi değer olarak geçirir. | | `BYREF` | `BYREF x AS tip` | Parametreyi referans/adres etkisiyle geçirir. | | `CDECL` | `CDECL` | C çağrı düzeni bilgisini belirtir. | | `STDCALL` | `STDCALL` | Windows API çağrı düzeni bilgisini belirtir. | İç içe çağrı örneği: ```basic id="5pwrp3" FUNCTION Add(a AS I32, b AS I32) AS I32 RETURN a + b END FUNCTION FUNCTION Mul(a AS I32, b AS I32) AS I32 RETURN a * b END FUNCTION PRINT Add(Mul(2, 3), Add(4, 5)) ``` Bu örnekte önce içteki çağrılar çözülür, sonra dıştaki `Add` çağrısı çalışır. AST bu yapıyı ağaç olarak taşır; MIR ise çağrı sırasını hedefe uygun ara temsil hâline getirir. ## 29.4. Operatör ailesi | Aile | Operatörler | Görev | |---|---|---| | Aritmetik | `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `\`, `MOD`, `**` | Sayısal hesap yapar. | | Karşılaştırma | `=`, `==`, `<>`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` | İki değeri karşılaştırır. | | Mantık | `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, `XOR` | Koşul veya bit düzeyinde mantıksal işlem yapar. | | Kaydırma | `SHL`, `SHR`, `ROL`, `ROR`, `<<`, `>>` | Bitleri sola, sağa veya döndürerek taşır. | | Logic16 | `NAND`, `NOR`, `XNOR`, `IMP`, `CIMP`, `NIMP`, `NCIMP`, `IDA`, `IDB`, `NOTA`, `NOTB` | Genişletilmiş mantık kapısı ailesidir. | | Atama | `=`, `+=`, `-=`, `*=`, `/=`, `%=`, `<<=`, `>>=`, `**=` | Değişkene yeni değer bağlar. | | Pipe | `|>` | Bir işlemin sonucunu sonraki işleme aktarma yüzeyi kurar. | | Üçlü | `?:` | Kısa koşullu ifade kurar. | Karşılaştırma notu önemlidir. `=` bağlama göre atama veya koşul eşitliği olarak görülebilir. Daha açık karşılaştırma için `==` kullanmak güvenlidir. ```basic id="h93g0w" DIM a AS I32 = 12 DIM b AS I32 = 5 PRINT a + b PRINT a AND b PRINT a OR b PRINT a XOR b PRINT a SHL 1 IF a >= b THEN PRINT "A_BUYUK" END IF ``` ## 29.5. Veri tipi ailesi | Tip | Görev | Kullanım | |---|---|---| | `I8`, `I16`, `I32`, `I64` | İşaretli tam sayı ailesidir. | Sayaç, miktar, indis | | `U8`, `U16`, `U32`, `U64` | İşaretsiz tam sayı ailesidir. | Bayt, maske, pozitif sayaç | | `F32`, `F64`, `F80`, `F128` | Kayan nokta ailesidir. | Ölçüm, oran, bilimsel hesap | | `BIGI`, `BIGINT` | Büyük tam sayı yüzeyidir. | Uzun tam sayı hesapları | | `BIGD`, `BIGF`, `BALL` | Geniş duyarlık / büyük ondalık yüzeyidir. | Para, hassas ölçüm, uzun hesap | | `BOOLEAN` | Doğru/yanlış değeri taşır. | Koşul, bayrak | | `STRING` | Metin taşır. | Ad, mesaj, dosya satırı | | `OBJECT` | Nesne yüzeyi taşır. | Sınıf, dış bağlama, genel nesne | | `PTR`, `STRPTR` | Adres ve metin işaretçisi yüzeyidir. | Dış fonksiyon, bellek işlemleri | Örnek: ```basic id="8sy6xp" DIM sayac AS I32 = 10 DIM ad AS STRING = "uXBasic" DIM aktif AS BOOLEAN = TRUE PRINT ad PRINT sayac ``` ## 29.6. Veri yapısı ailesi | Yapı | Syntax | Görev | |---|---|---| | Dizi | `DIM a(10) AS I32` | Aynı tipten çoklu değerleri indeksle saklar. | | `TYPE` | `TYPE Ad ... END TYPE` | Alanlardan oluşan kayıt tipi tanımlar. | | `CLASS` | `CLASS Ad ... END CLASS` | Veri ve davranışı birlikte taşıyan nesne tipi kurar. | | `INTERFACE` | `INTERFACE Ad ... END INTERFACE` | Davranış sözleşmesi tanımlar. | | `ARRAY` | `ARRAY OF tip` | Koleksiyon tip yüzeyi olarak dizi ailesini belirtir. | | `LIST` | `LIST OF tip` | Sıralı büyüyebilir liste yüzeyi kurar. | | `DICT` | `DICT OF anahtar, değer` | Anahtar-değer eşleme yüzeyi kurar. | | `SET` | `SET OF tip` | Benzersiz eleman kümesi yüzeyi kurar. | | `MODULE` | `MODULE Ad ... END MODULE` | Büyük kodu modül başlığı altında toplar. | | `NAMESPACE` | `NAMESPACE Ad ... END NAMESPACE` | İsim çakışmasını önleyen kapsam alanı kurar. | `TYPE` örneği: ```basic id="rsaf7e" TYPE Nokta x AS I32 y AS I32 END TYPE DIM p AS Nokta p.x = 12 p.y = 30 PRINT p.x + p.y ``` `CLASS` ve `MAGIC` örneği: ```basic id="o8qk6n" CLASS Anahtar VALUE AS I32 MAGIC HASH() AS I32 RETURN VALUE + 100 END MAGIC MAGIC ADD(other AS I32) AS I32 RETURN VALUE + other END MAGIC END CLASS ``` Burada `MAGIC`, sınıf içinde özel davranış sözleşmesi açar. Bu bölümde `MAGIC` sıradan fonksiyon adı gibi değil, nesne davranış kapısı olarak anlatılır. --- # 30. Preprocessor A/B ve Hedefli Derleme uXBasic preprocessor, kaynak kodun derleyiciye gitmeden önceki aklını temsil eder. Normal komutlar program çalışırken davranır; preprocessor yönergeleri ise kaynak dosya daha lexer katmanına gitmeden önce çalışır. Bu yüzden `%%IF` ile `IF` aynı şey değildir. `IF` runtime karar yapısıdır; `%%IF` kaynak seçme yapısıdır. uXBasic içinde preprocessor hattı iki ana seçenekle kullanılır: ```text id="h80vm1" --pp A --pp B ``` A hattı ana preprocess yoludur. B hattı genişletilmiş blok, web, manifest, asset ve hedef odaklı kullanım için tasarlanan ayrı yoldur. Kaynak içinde `%%PP B` benzeri seçimler veya CLI üzerinden `--pp B` kullanımı, kitapta hedefli preprocess örnekleri için özellikle anlatılır. ## 30.1. Değer tanımlama | Yönerge | Syntax | Görev | |---|---|---| | `%%SET` | `%%SET AD = değer` | Meta değişken tanımlar veya değer atar. | | `%%DEFINE` | `%%DEFINE AD değer` | Preprocess sembolü veya sabiti tanımlar. | | `%%UNDEF` | `%%UNDEF AD` | Önceden tanımlanmış sembolü kaldırır. | | `%%EVAL` | `%%EVAL AD = ifade` | Meta ifadeyi hesaplayıp sonuç üretir. | Örnek: ```basic id="rqxmuw" %%SET MOD = "DEBUG" %%DEFINE LIMIT 100 %%EVAL CIFT_LIMIT = LIMIT * 2 %%IF MOD == "DEBUG" PRINT "DEBUG_ACIK" %%ENDIF ``` Bu örnekte `MOD`, `LIMIT` ve `CIFT_LIMIT` runtime değişkeni değildir. Bunlar kaynak hazırlanırken kullanılır. ## 30.2. Koşullu kaynak seçme | Yönerge | Görev | |---|---| | `%%IF` | Koşul doğruysa bloğu kaynakta bırakır. | | `%%IFC` | Koşullu kontrol için ek yüzey sağlar. | | `%%IFN` | Olumsuz koşul kontrolü kurar. | | `%%ELIF` | Önceki koşul yanlışsa yeni koşul dener. | | `%%ELSE` | Hiçbir koşul sağlanmazsa seçilecek bloktur. | | `%%ENDIF` | Koşullu preprocess bloğunu kapatır. | Örnek: ```basic id="zm2upl" %%SET HEDEF = "TEST" %%IF HEDEF == "TEST" PRINT "TEST_SURUMU" %%ELIF HEDEF == "WEB" PRINT "WEB_SURUMU" %%ELSE PRINT "NORMAL_SURUM" %%ENDIF ``` Bu yapı, tek kaynak dosyadan farklı hedefler üretmeye yarar. Kitapta “öneri” olarak bırakılmaz; doğrudan bu örnekle gösterilir. ## 30.3. Döngülü preprocess Preprocessor döngüleri tekrar eden kaynak parçalarını üretmek için kullanılır. Bu aile özellikle tablo, manifest, test dosyası, tekrar eden sabit ve hedef çıktısı oluştururken işe yarar. | Yönerge | Görev | |---|---| | `%%FOR` | Sayısal veya sembolik tekrar başlatır. | | `%%FOREACH` | Liste üzerinde tekrar kurar. | | `%%REPEAT` | Belirli sayıda tekrar üretir. | | `%%ENDFOR` | Döngü bloğunu kapatır. | | `%%BREAK` | Preprocess döngüsünü erken keser. | | `%%CONTINUE` | Sonraki preprocess tekrarına geçer. | Kullanım fikri: ```basic id="aujrz0" %%FOR I = 1 TO 3 PRINT "SATIR" %%ENDFOR ``` Bu satırlar runtime `FOR` döngüsü değildir. Preprocessor bu bloğu kaynakta çoğaltır. Runtime döngüyle arasındaki fark kitapta özellikle vurgulanmalıdır. ## 30.4. Hedef seçme | Yönerge | Görev | |---|---| | `%%TARGET` | Üretim hedefini belirtir: konsol, web, browser, wasm gibi. | | `%%PLATFORM` | Platform bilgisini kaynak seçiminde kullanır. | | `%%DESTOS` | Hedef işletim sistemi bilgisini taşır. | | `%%PROFILE` | Debug, release, test gibi profil mantığını kurar. | | `%%OUTDIR` | Üretilen artefactların çıkış klasörünü belirler. | Örnek: ```basic id="sq8hd1" %%TARGET WEB %%PROFILE "DEBUG" %%OUTDIR "dist/debug_web" PRINT "HEDEF_WEB" ``` Bu örnek kaynak kodun kendisini değiştirmeden hedef bilgisini değiştirir. CLI tarafında aynı fikir `--target`, `--out-root`, `--artifact-root`, `--emit-js`, `--emit-wat`, `--emit-browser` gibi seçeneklerle tamamlanır. ## 30.5. HTML, CSS ve JS blokları Web hedefinde preprocessor yalnız koşul seçmez; dosya üreten bloklar da açabilir. | Yönerge | Görev | |---|---| | `%%HTML_BEGIN` / `%%HTML_END` | HTML artefact bloğu üretir. | | `%%CSS_BEGIN` / `%%CSS_END` | CSS artefact bloğu üretir. | | `%%JS_BEGIN` / `%%JS_END` | JS artefact bloğu üretir. | | `%%JS_LINE` | Tek satırlık JS üretim yüzeyi sağlar. | Örnek: ```basic id="6r10fc" %%TARGET WEB %%OUTDIR "dist/web_panel" %%HTML_BEGIN "index.html" BODY

uXBasic Panel

%%HTML_END %%CSS_BEGIN "style.css" body { font-family: sans-serif; } %%CSS_END %%JS_BEGIN "program.js" RUNTIME console.log("PANEL_BASLADI"); %%JS_END PRINT "WEB_ARTEFACT_OK" ``` Burada `PRINT` hâlâ uXBasic komutudur; HTML/CSS/JS blokları ise preprocess/backend artefact üretimiyle ilgilidir. ## 30.6. WAT/WASM blokları | Yönerge | Görev | |---|---| | `%%WAT_BEGIN` / `%%WAT_END` | WAT metin bloğu açar ve kapatır. | | `%%WAT_FUNC_BEGIN` / `%%WAT_FUNC_END` | WAT fonksiyon bloğu üretir. | | `%%WAT_IMPORT` | WAT/WASM dış import tanımlar. | | `%%WAT_EXPORT` | WAT/WASM dış export tanımlar. | WAT örneği: ```basic id="jc5g9i" %%TARGET WASM %%OUTDIR "dist/wasm_demo" %%WAT_BEGIN "module.wat" (module (func $answer (result i32) i32.const 42) (export "answer" (func $answer)) ) %%WAT_END PRINT "WAT_ROUTE" ``` Bu örnek WAT yüzeyini gösterir. Kitapta WAT/WASM hedefleri anlatılırken MIR destekli backend üretimiyle bu raw hedef blokları birbirinden ayırt edilmelidir. ## 30.7. Asset ve manifest ailesi | Yönerge | Görev | |---|---| | `%%ASSET_ROOT` | Varlık dosyalarının kök klasörünü belirler. | | `%%ASSET_FILE` | Tek dosyayı artefact listesine ekler. | | `%%ASSET_COPY` | Varlık dosyasını çıktı klasörüne kopyalama yüzeyi kurar. | | `%%ASSET_IMAGE` | Görsel varlık bildirir. | | `%%ASSET_AUDIO` | Ses varlığı bildirir. | | `%%MANIFEST_SET` | Manifest alanı yazar. | | `%%MANIFEST_REQUIRE` | Zorunlu manifest alanı ister. | | `%%JSON_SET` | JSON alanı üretir. | | `%%JSON_BEGIN` / `%%JSON_END` | JSON blok üretimi yapar. | Örnek: ```basic id="mdcnr7" %%TARGET WEB %%OUTDIR "dist/assets_demo" %%ASSET_ROOT "assets" %%ASSET_IMAGE "logo.png" %%MANIFEST_SET name = "uXBasicDemo" %%JSON_SET version = "12.06_1" PRINT "ASSET_MANIFEST_OK" ``` Bu aile özellikle browser, oyun, eğitim aracı veya küçük web paneli üretirken kullanılır. ## 30.8. Güvenlik ve kapı yönergeleri Raw JS, raw WAT, include ve host binding gibi alanlar güçlüdür; bu yüzden güvenlik kapılarıyla birlikte düşünülür. | Yönerge | Görev | |---|---| | `%%ALLOW_RAW_JS` | Raw JS bloklarının kullanılmasına izin kapısı açar. | | `%%ALLOW_RAW_WAT` | Raw WAT bloklarının kullanılmasına izin kapısı açar. | | `%%SAFE_PATHS` | Güvenli dosya yolu sınırlarını belirtir. | | `%%REQUIRE_HOST_BINDING` | Host tarafında gerekli bağlamı şart koşar. | Kural şudur: hedefsiz raw kod serbest bırakılmaz. Bu kitap, güçlü kapıları gizlemez; fakat her güçlü kapının hangi hedef ve izinle kullanılacağını açık yazar. --- # 31. Backend ve Artefact Üretim Rehberi uXBasic’in güçlü tarafı yalnız kaynak kodu yorumlamak değildir. Aynı kaynak, hedefe göre farklı artefactlar üretebilir. Bu bölümde AST, MIR, runtime ve backend ilişkisi üzerinden JS, WAT/WASM ve x64 üretim hattı anlatılır. Ana ilke değişmez: ```text id="og7vwe" AST kaynak anlamını taşır. MIR hedef üretim omurgasıdır. AST interpreter AST üzerinden çalışır. MIR interpreter MIR üzerinden çalışır. JS, WAT/WASM ve x64 üretimi MIR seviyesinden destek alır. x64 kod üretimi MIR seviyesindedir; AST kaynak anlamıyla yardımcı olur. ``` ## 31.1. AST ve MIR farkını örnekle görmek Kaynak kod: ```basic id="tz59ck" DIM a AS I32 = 10 DIM b AS I32 = 20 PRINT a + b ``` AST bu kodu kaynak anlamına yakın taşır: değişken tanımı, atama, ifade ve `PRINT` düğümü vardır. AST interpreter ve MIR interpreter AST yorumlayıcı doğrudan AST üzerinden yürür: ```powershell id="21bo9j" .\bin\uxb.exe .\bin\demo.uxb --execmem --interpreter-backend AST --stdout-out reports\ast_stdout.txt ``` MIR yorumlayıcı MIR üzerinden yürür: ```powershell id="u63ngh" .\bin\uxb.exe .\bin\demo.uxb --execmem --interpreter-backend MIR --mir-program-output-out reports\mir_output.txt ``` İkisi aynı çıktıyı üretmelidir. JS hedefi JS hedefi için: ```powershell id="w85572" .\bin\uxb.exe .\bin\demo.uxb --emit-js --js-out dist\program.js --js-runtime-out dist\uxb_runtime.js ``` Bu komut JS dosyası üretir. JS hedefi anlatılırken iki ayrı yol karıştırılmaz: uXBasic komutlarının JS’e çevrilmesi ayrı, preprocess ile raw JS bloğu yazılması ayrıdır. ## 31.4. Browser hedefi Browser hedefi HTML ve JS artefactlarını birlikte düşünebilir: ```powershell id="6ekqty" .\bin\uxb.exe .\bin\demo.uxb --emit-browser --html-out dist\index.html --js-out dist\program.js --js-runtime-out dist\uxb_runtime.js ``` Preprocessor web bloklarıyla birlikte örnek: ```basic id="01qeps" %%TARGET WEB %%OUTDIR "dist/browser_demo" %%HTML_BEGIN "index.html" BODY

uXBasic Browser

%%HTML_END %%JS_BEGIN "program.js" RUNTIME console.log("BROWSER_OK"); %%JS_END PRINT "WEB_ROUTE" ``` ## 31.5. ## Güncel ABI10 ve güvenlik sözleşmesi

Güncel Windows x64 dış çağrı sözleşmesi `uxffi` API 131 ve en çok 10 argümandır. Desteklenen dönüş tipleri `VOID, I32, U32, I64, U64, F64, PTR, STRPTR`; argüman tipleri `I32, U32, I64, U64, F64, PTR, STRPTR`; çağrı düzenleri `CDECL` ve `STDCALL` biçimindedir. Pointer sonuçları ham adres olarak değil generation kontrollü opaque token olarak taşınır. `STRPTR` sonucu çağrı kilidi açıkken dinamik bir uXBasic metnine kopyalanır.

Önerilen açık tipli biçim:

```basic
sonuc = CALL(DLL, "kutuphane.dll", "fonksiyon", I32, CDECL, "I32,STRPTR", sayi, metin)
```

10	
11	**Context**: this decision closes out [[uxb-fix-plan-decisions-2026-09]]'s S-036 (MEMCOPYD silently copying zeros) by settling a much bigger, previously-unresolved architecture question the user had been carrying since the language's early design phase. The user presented (2026-09-13/14) a long, well-researched chronological analysis of how uXBasic's memory model evolved (1 MiB toy virtual RAM → hybrid `<1MiB=virtual/>=1MiB=real` heuristic in the x64 backend → NATIVE/VIRTUAL/EXTERNAL concept discussed 2026-08-09 but never fully implemented → today's S-036 discovery that arrays have NO real backing address at all in most engines). Codex independently converged on the same target design from the same document (posted to `ai_koordinasyon/SORULAR_CEVAPLAR.md`, includes a `MemoryRef` abstraction proposal). This memory is the durable record of the LOCKED design; see the coordination log for the full back-and-forth.
12	
13	## The locked design
14	
15	1. **NATIVE is the primary model, not a fallback.** `VARPTR`, pointer arithmetic, `PEEK*`/`POKE*`, `MEMCOPY*`/`MEMFILL*` operate on real, addressable process memory by default. A uXBasic program cannot PEEK/POKE arbitrary OS/physical RAM (Windows user-mode has no such right without drivers) — "real memory" means "this process's own address space."
16	2. **Arrays (including STRUCT-element arrays) get exactly ONE real backing storage, never a second VM-mirrored copy.** `VARPTR(array)` = the address of that one real buffer (= `VARPTR(array(LBOUND(array)))`). Indexed reads/writes (`a(i)=x`), `PEEK*`/`POKE*` through `VARPTR`, and `MEMCOPY*`/`MEMFILL*` through that same address must all observe each other's effects immediately — no "copy into VM, forget to sync back" failure mode (that IS S-036's root cause, confirmed independently by both Claude 1's AST-interpreter trace and Codex's own source reading).
17	3. **VIRTUAL is an explicit, opt-in, separate address space** — not triggered by address magnitude (the current x64 `<1MiB` heuristic in `__uxb_mem_resolve` is explicitly rejected as bad design). Selected via the `NATIVE`/`VIRTUAL` mode keyword that already exists in the parser/AST for `PEEK*`/`POKE*`/`MEMCOPY*`/`MEMFILL*` (`ExecMemoryModeOffset` in `exec_stmt_memory_core.fbs`) — today the AST interpreter's `NATIVE` mode is deliberately rejected ("NATIVE memory is unavailable in interpreter"); that rejection must be lifted since NATIVE is now the default/primary path.
18	4. **EXTERNAL is not a separate technical region** — a DLL/API-returned buffer address is just an ordinary real address inside NATIVE's address space; no separate code path needed beyond "don't refuse it."
19	5. **New user-requested feature, layered on top of #3**: VIRTUAL's size is configurable, and can optionally extend onto disk. Locked syntax: `VIRTUAL <ramSize>[, <diskSize>]` as a real BASIC statement (e.g. `VIRTUAL 2M, 16G` = 2 MB RAM-backed + 16 GB disk-backed extension), size suffixes `K`/`M`/`G` are 1024-based. A CLI flag with the identical syntax (`--virtual=2M,16G`) sets the program's default before it starts; the in-program `VIRTUAL` statement can (re)configure it at runtime (re-issuing it discards prior VIRTUAL-space contents, like `REDIM` without `PRESERVE` — no live-resize-preserving-data complexity). Disk-backed portion should use a Windows memory-mapped file (`CreateFileMapping`/`MapViewOfFile`) rather than a hand-rolled swap system — let the OS's own paging handle the RAM/disk tradeoff transparently.
20	6. **Pointer arithmetic is byte-based always** (`p + 1` = next byte, never "next element of whatever type"). For typed array element addressing: `address = baseAddress + (index - lowerBound) * elementStride`, and `elementStride` must be the type's real `SIZEOF`, never a hardcoded assumption (Codex found at least one place in the x64 static-array backend that hardcodes 8 bytes regardless of element type — must be found and fixed as part of this).
21	7. **No width loss in the PEEK/POKE/MEMCOPY/MEMFILL family.** Codex found that the x64 MIR runtime-call layer collapses `PEEKB/W/D` → a single 64-bit `MIRX64EmitRuntimePeekI64`/`PokeI64` helper regardless of the requested width — this silently discards width information at exactly the wrong layer and must be fixed so B/W/D widths survive all the way to the actual memory access. A new **Q (64-bit) family** (`PEEKQ`/`POKEQ`/`MEMCOPYQ`/`MEMFILLQ`) should be added alongside B/W/D for completeness, now that uXBasic is a real x64-targeting language.
22	8. **MEMCOPY's canonical argument order is locked as `dst, src, count`** (matches the docs and the MIR contract). A real, independent, already-found inconsistency: the legacy AST-direct x64 backend's `X64EmitMemCopyStmt` treats its operands as `src, dst, len` — the reverse — and must be corrected to match.
23	9. **LIST/DICT/SET remain excluded from raw memory access** (no `VARPTR`/`PEEK`/`POKE`/`MEMCOPY` on their internal GLib-backed representation) — this boundary was already correct and stays as-is; only `ARRAY`/`STRUCT`/`STRUCT ARRAY`/scalars/POD-like types get a raw memory view.
24	10. **`REDIM` may relocate an array's backing storage; a `VARPTR` taken before `REDIM` is not guaranteed valid after it** (documented `realloc`-like semantics, not a bug to "fix" by adding pointer-tracking machinery — deliberately kept simple).
25	11. **Codex's proposed unifying abstraction**: a shared `MemoryRef` record (`kind`, `owner`, `baseAddress`, `byteOffset`, `byteLength`, `elementStride`, `writable`, `generation`) that every memory-touching op (`VARPTR`/`PEEK*`/`POKE*`/`MEMCOPY*`/`MEMFILL*`) resolves through via one `ResolveMemoryRef()`, instead of each op re-deriving "is this scalar/array/struct" independently. Agreed as the right END STATE, but Claude 1's stated implementation order is: get each engine's OBSERVABLE behavior correct first (single array backing storage, no width loss, correct stride) via more surgical per-engine fixes, THEN fold the logic into the shared abstraction if it doesn't cost another full pass — reversing that order risks a long half-finished refactor that runs nothing correctly in the meantime.
26	
27	## Implementation order Claude 1 committed to (smallest/independent first)
28	
29	(a) MEMCOPY canonical parameter order fix + add the Q (64-bit) family.
30	(b) Fix x64's PEEK/POKE width collapsing to 64-bit at the MIR runtime-call layer.
31	(c) **The S-036 core**: give the AST interpreter's arrays one real, contiguous backing buffer; make `VARPTR`/`PEEK*`/`POKE*`/`MEMCOPY*` read/write that same buffer instead of a disconnected VM space.
32	(d) Same for the canonical-MIR interpreter (`MIRValue elements()`-based array storage today; needs the same single-backing-storage treatment).

Canonical-MIR: handled in `mir_interp_memory.fbs`'s `UXBMIRInterpExecMemory` specifically because that's an `st`-receiving handler group (`MIR_EXPR`'s `UXBMIRInterpExecArith` does NOT receive `st`, so could never have implemented this) — takes the real address of the variable's `UXBInterpValue` field via `@`, with the same documented caveat AST arrays have for REDIM: `st.vars()` is dynamically `ReDim`'d and scope-exit-compacted, so the address is only valid within the variable's own scope. Native x64: turned out `VARPTR` already canonicalizes to `"ADDR_OF"` and a `CODEPTR/LPTR/ADDR_OF` emitter case already existed (`mir_x64_opcode_surface_emitters.fbs`) but had two latent bugs (never stripped the quoted operand; only checked local variables, never globals) — fixed by routing it through the already-correct `MIRX64AddressOfVarToReg`.
62	- **Canonical-MIR's NATIVE memory family had the exact same blanket rejection AST had before its own fix**: `runtime_memory.fbs`'s `UXBRuntimeMemoryLoadWidth/StoreWidth/CopyMode/FillMode` all did `If modeId = 2 (NATIVE) Then Return 0`. Fixed with the same `IsBadReadPtr`/`IsBadWritePtr`-validated real-pointer approach as AST (the two engines now share one `Declare` for these Win32 functions — FreeBASIC's single combined translation unit rejects declaring the same extern twice, so only `runtime_memory.fbs` keeps the Declare now).
63	- **Verified**: the same VARPTR+NATIVE MEMCOPYD/POKED/PEEKD test now gives byte-identical correct output across AST, canonical-MIR, and native x64. 33/33 regression suite green throughout; legacy AST-direct x64 (`--x64-mode AST`) and all earlier array tests re-verified unaffected. `bin/uxb.exe` SHA256 after all S-049 work: `AE35103A3EF63A047FE95B57BE85C5F30573D9329E71EC3A864CD4B80FA2983C`.
64	- **Struct-array (array of TYPE) field access investigated (S-050): the suspected AST "sync" bug was a false alarm** (AST already reads/writes `pts(i).X`-style consistently) — but investigating it surfaced a real, different bug: **canonical-MIR's `pts(i).X` with a runtime-variable index always returned 0** (worked fine with a literal index). Root cause: field access on an indexed-array-of-struct baked the index EXPRESSION'S TEXT (not its runtime value) into a compile-time flat pseudo-variable name like `"PTS(I).X"` — literal indices worked by coincidence (same text on write and read), a variable index could never match. **Fixed** (user approved the "big/correct" option over a narrower patch): added `MIR_ARRAY_FIELD_LOAD`/`MIR_ARRAY_FIELD_STORE` opcodes that route through the array+object heap model already used by plain numeric arrays and CLASS objects (`UXBInterpHeapGetIndex`/`SetIndex`/`GetField`/`SetField`), lazily materializing an element as a heap OBJECT the first time it's touched this way. Found yet another instance of this session's recurring "hidden duplicate file" bug pattern doing this: `ASSIGN_STMT` lowering is duplicated verbatim across `mir_lower_stmt.fbs` and `mir_lower_stmt_core_split.fbs` — both had to be fixed. Only plain `=` assignment was fixed (compound ops like `+=` on an array-of-struct field still use the old, literal-index-only path — unchanged from before, not a new regression). Verified identical to AST across a read+write+FOR-loop test; CLASS fields and plain arrays unaffected; 33/33 regression green. Separately noted, explicitly out of scope: native x64 (default `bld` backend) doesn't support struct arrays AT ALL yet (a compile-time "unsupported array element type" error, not a silent-wrong-result -- an honest, different gap).
65	- **Still not done as of this line**: the new `VIRTUAL <ram>[,<disk>]` statement + CLI flag + disk-backed extension (not started); native x64 struct-array support (not started, separate feature gap); compound-assignment (`+=` etc.) on array-of-struct fields in canonical-MIR (still literal-index-only).
66	
67	**Same-day follow-up #2 (2026-09-14, locked-design step (f), AST-interpreter + CLI scope only):**
68	
69	**The new `VIRTUAL <ramSize>[, <diskSize>]` statement: ✅ done and verified for the AST interpreter (`run`) and its CLI default flag — canonical-MIR and native x64 NOT started (deliberately: native x64 files are Codex's active S-050 CLAIM this same day; canonical-MIR's own `runtime_memory.fbs` still uses a fixed `(0 To 1048575)` static array, untouched).**
70	- **Parser**: new `ASTK_VIRTUAL_STMT` node kind, `STMT_HANDLER_VIRTUAL` dispatch entry, `ParseVirtualStmt` (`parser_stmt_basic.fbs`) — accepts `VIRTUAL <ram>[, <disk>]`, each operand a bare NUMBER token (optionally K/M/G/T-suffixed, e.g. `2M`). Deliberately did NOT touch the shared lexer/expression pipeline to make suffixed literals "just work" everywhere — the raw token lexeme is stored verbatim on the AST node, and K/M/G/T→bytes scaling (1024-based) happens only at statement-execution time, in a new `ExecParseByteSizeLiteral` (`exec_stmt_memory_core.fbs`).
71	- **`memory_vm.fbs` rewritten from a RAM-only sandbox into RAM+disk**: `[0, ramBytes)` is the existing RAM `UByte` array; `[ramBytes, ramBytes+diskBytes)` is a NEW disk-backed extension via a real Windows memory-mapped temp file (`CreateFileA` + `CreateFileMappingA` + `MapViewOfFile`, opened with `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_TEMPORARY | FILE_FLAG_DELETE_ON_CLOSE` so the OS deletes it automatically once every handle closes — no hand-rolled swap system, exactly as the locked design specified). Every `VMemPeek*/Poke*/Copy*/Fill*` now goes through one indirection, `VMemByteAt(addr) As UByte Ptr`, that resolves to either the RAM array or the mapped view. `VMemInit` changed from a parameterless `Sub` to a `Function VMemInit(ramBytes, diskBytes, ByRef errText, ...) As Integer` returning success/failure (confirmed via an isolated scratch test that FreeBASIC does allow a default on a `ByRef String` parameter). Re-issuing `VMemInit`/`VIRTUAL` releases the old mapping/temp file first and re-inits everything from zero — matches "REDIM without PRESERVE" semantics exactly as locked, deliberately not preserving old contents.
72	- **CLI flag `--virtual=<ram>[,<disk>]`**: added to the CLI registry (`cli_registry_adim41.fbs`, option count 171→172). Wiring it to `VMemInit` needed a small workaround: `GetArgValue` (declared in `main_cli_runtime_helpers.fbs`) is textually `#include`'d AFTER `memory_exec.fbs` in the build's single combined translation unit, so it can't be called directly from `ExecRunMemoryProgram`. Fixed with a global, `gUxbCliVirtualArg As String` (declared early, in `memory_exec.fbs`, before it's needed), set once in `main_program_entry.fbs` right after CLI parsing becomes available, and read by `ExecRunMemoryProgram` before running any program statement — the in-program `VIRTUAL` statement can still destructively override this CLI-set default at runtime, exactly as designed.
73	- **A real language-behavior gotcha hit while testing, NOT a bug in this feature**: in this dialect, suffixless `POKE`/`PEEK` default to a 4-byte (dword) operation — `PEEK`/`PEEKD` literally share one code path (`Case "PEEK", "PEEKD"` in `exec_eval_builtin_categories.fbs`). An early test wrote a dword at the RAM region's very last byte address and got a correct "out of range" rejection that briefly looked like a VIRTUAL bug; it wasn't — byte-level ops need `POKEB`/`PEEKB` explicitly. Worth remembering before assuming any future off-by-N report near a VIRTUAL boundary is this feature's fault.
74	- **Verified by real compile+run**: RAM-only (`VIRTUAL 2M`) byte and dword poke/peek plus `MEMCOPYB`, all correct. RAM+disk (`VIRTUAL 1M, 4M`): both regions independently read/write correctly, including the disk region's very first and very last byte. Writing one byte past the total (RAM+disk) size fails with a clean `exec:` error, not a crash. Re-issuing `VIRTUAL` mid-program correctly discards all prior RAM+disk contents. `--virtual=1M,4M` sets the CLI default correctly, and an in-program `VIRTUAL 512K` correctly and destructively overrides it (the old disk address becomes out-of-range afterward, as expected). 33/33 regression suite green both with and without `--virtual=`. Full evidence: `ai_koordinasyon/SORUN_TAKIP.md` S-049 item 3.
75	
76	**Same-day follow-up #3 (2026-09-15): VIRTUAL statement is now DONE across all 4 engines.** Codex wired canonical-MIR (`MIR_VIRTUAL_INIT` opcode, `mir_interp_memory.fbs` reuses the AST's own `VMemInit`/`memory_vm.fbs` directly — `runtime_memory.fbs`'s old fixed `gUXBRuntimeVirtualMemory` array is now genuinely dead) and native x64 (`__uxb_mem_virtual_init` in `mir_x64_context.fbs`, real `CreateFileMappingA`/`MapViewOfFile` for dynamic RAM+disk) overnight. Claude 1 found and fixed 3 real bugs surfaced by this new code while verifying it: (1) **S-057** — out-of-range VIRTUAL access silently returned `0` on native x64 (and, a twin bug, `-1` unchecked on AST's PEEK-family expression forms) instead of a real error; fixed via a checked-call wrapper (`MIRX64EmitMemoryModeCallChecked`) that clears/checks the sticky `__uxb_mem_error` flag around every `__uxb_mem_*_mode` call, mirroring the pattern S-019's native collection ABI already established. (2) A genuine SIGFPE crash (divide-by-zero) in both `UXBMIRInterpParseVirtualBytes` and its byte-for-byte duplicate `MIRX64VirtualSizeLiteral` — Codex's new overflow check used `If n<>0 And mult > ... \ n`, and FreeBASIC's `And` does not short-circuit, so the division ran even when n=0 (the default disk-size text when `VIRTUAL <ram>` is given with no disk argument). Fixed by nesting the `n<>0` check. (3) **S-063** — calling `VIRTUAL` a second time in the same program (the REDIM-without-PRESERVE re-init path) crashed native x64 with a real `0xC0000005`: `__uxb_mem_virtual_init`'s prologue never restored 16-byte stack alignment after its two `push` instructions (function entry is 8-mod-16 per the x64 ABI's own call convention; two pushes, an even count, don't change that), so every WinAPI call inside it was 8 bytes misaligned — `CreateFileMappingA`/`MapViewOfFile` happened not to fault on it, `UnmapViewOfFile`/`CloseHandle` (only reached on a second+ VIRTUAL call, releasing the old mapping) reliably did. Fixed with an extra `sub rsp,8` at entry and matching `add rsp,8` before both returns. **Verified**: a full write+read+reinit+read scenario now gives byte-identical `111,222,111,0` across AST/canonical-MIR/native-x64; 33/33 regression green throughout. Remaining, separately-tracked, non-blocking findings from this same investigation: S-058 (AST's NATIVE memory addresses are 32-bit `UInteger` while canonical-MIR uses 64-bit `ULongInt`), S-059 (NATIVE `POKES`/`PEEKS` accepted/rejected inconsistently across the 3 native-capable backends), S-061 (a negative-valued DWORD PEEK prints as unsigned `4294967295` on AST/canonical-MIR but signed `-1` on native x64 — a display/CInt inconsistency, not a memory-safety bug), S-062 (the legacy, non-default `--x64-mode AST` backend's own mode-blind PEEK/POKE resolver has no bounds check at all above 1MiB and treats the raw address as a native pointer — a different, deeper issue in a different, non-default backend, deliberately left alone this turn). Full detail: `ai_koordinasyon/SORUN_TAKIP.md` S-057/S-063, and the new cross-cutting plan `docs/UXB_ACIK_ISLER_TASARIM_VE_UYGULAMA_PLANI_20260915_TR.md`.
77	
78	Update this section further with ✅/dates/hashes as each remaining step (S-033/034/035/055/056, S-058/059/061/062) lands, the same way [[uxb-fix-plan-decisions-2026-09]] tracks S-019/S-032/S-046/S-047.

file.content:
---
name: uxb-memory-architecture-2026-09
description: "uXBasic's locked-in low-level memory model (NATIVE/VIRTUAL/EXTERNAL, single array backing storage, byte-based pointers) decided 2026-09-14 for S-036; implementation progress log."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 760ce433-ff72-46c7-8b20-30eed40f7a8c
  modified: 2026-09-14T22:43:43.868Z
---

**Context**: this decision closes out [[uxb-fix-plan-decisions-2026-09]]'s S-036 (MEMCOPYD silently copying zeros) by settling a much bigger, previously-unresolved architecture question the user had been carrying since the language's early design phase. The user presented (2026-09-13/14) a long, well-researched chronological analysis of how uXBasic's memory model evolved (1 MiB toy virtual RAM → hybrid `<1MiB=virtual/>=1MiB=real` heuristic in the x64 backend → NATIVE/VIRTUAL/EXTERNAL concept discussed 2026-08-09 but never fully implemented → today's S-036 discovery that arrays have NO real backing address at all in most engines). Codex independently converged on the same target design from the same document (posted to `ai_koordinasyon/SORULAR_CEVAPLAR.md`, includes a `MemoryRef` abstraction proposal). This memory is the durable record of the LOCKED design; see the coordination log for the full back-and-forth.

## The locked design

1. **NATIVE is the primary model, not a fallback.** `VARPTR`, pointer arithmetic, `PEEK*`/`POKE*`, `MEMCOPY*`/`MEMFILL*` operate on real, addressable process memory by default. A uXBasic program cannot PEEK/POKE arbitrary OS/physical RAM (Windows user-mode has no such right without drivers) — "real memory" means "this process's own address space."
2. **Arrays (including STRUCT-element arrays) get exactly ONE real backing storage, never a second VM-mirrored copy.** `VARPTR(array)` = the address of that one real buffer (= `VARPTR(array(LBOUND(array)))`). Indexed reads/writes (`a(i)=x`), `PEEK*`/`POKE*` through `VARPTR`, and `MEMCOPY*`/`MEMFILL*` through that same address must all observe each other's effects immediately — no "copy into VM, forget to sync back" failure mode (that IS S-036's root cause, confirmed independently by both Claude 1's AST-interpreter trace and Codex's own source reading).
3. **VIRTUAL is an explicit, opt-in, separate address space** — not triggered by address magnitude (the current x64 `<1MiB` heuristic in `__uxb_mem_resolve` is explicitly rejected as bad design). Selected via the `NATIVE`/`VIRTUAL` mode keyword that already exists in the parser/AST for `PEEK*`/`POKE*`/`MEMCOPY*`/`MEMFILL*` (`ExecMemoryModeOffset` in `exec_stmt_memory_core.fbs`) — today the AST interpreter's `NATIVE` mode is deliberately rejected ("NATIVE memory is unavailable in interpreter"); that rejection must be lifted since NATIVE is now the default/primary path.
4. **EXTERNAL is not a separate technical region** — a DLL/API-returned buffer address is just an ordinary real address inside NATIVE's address space; no separate code path needed beyond "don't refuse it."
5. **New user-requested feature, layered on top of #3**: VIRTUAL's size is configurable, and can optionally extend onto disk. Locked syntax: `VIRTUAL <ramSize>[, <diskSize>]` as a real BASIC statement (e.g. `VIRTUAL 2M, 16G` = 2 MB RAM-backed + 16 GB disk-backed extension), size suffixes `K`/`M`/`G` are 1024-based. A CLI flag with the identical syntax (`--virtual=2M,16G`) sets the program's default before it starts; the in-program `VIRTUAL` statement can (re)configure it at runtime (re-issuing it discards prior VIRTUAL-space contents, like `REDIM` without `PRESERVE` — no live-resize-preserving-data complexity). Disk-backed portion should use a Windows memory-mapped file (`CreateFileMapping`/`MapViewOfFile`) rather than a hand-rolled swap system — let the OS's own paging handle the RAM/disk tradeoff transparently.
6. **Pointer arithmetic is byte-based always** (`p + 1` = next byte, never "next element of whatever type"). For typed array element addressing: `address = baseAddress + (index - lowerBound) * elementStride`, and `elementStride` must be the type's real `SIZEOF`, never a hardcoded assumption (Codex found at least one place in the x64 static-array backend that hardcodes 8 bytes regardless of element type — must be found and fixed as part of this).
7. **No width loss in the PEEK/POKE/MEMCOPY/MEMFILL family.** Codex found that the x64 MIR runtime-call layer collapses `PEEKB/W/D` → a single 64-bit `MIRX64EmitRuntimePeekI64`/`PokeI64` helper regardless of the requested width — this silently discards width information at exactly the wrong layer and must be fixed so B/W/D widths survive all the way to the actual memory access. A new **Q (64-bit) family** (`PEEKQ`/`POKEQ`/`MEMCOPYQ`/`MEMFILLQ`) should be added alongside B/W/D for completeness, now that uXBasic is a real x64-targeting language.
8. **MEMCOPY's canonical argument order is locked as `dst, src, count`** (matches the docs and the MIR contract). A real, independent, already-found inconsistency: the legacy AST-direct x64 backend's `X64EmitMemCopyStmt` treats its operands as `src, dst, len` — the reverse — and must be corrected to match.
9. **LIST/DICT/SET remain excluded from raw memory access** (no `VARPTR`/`PEEK`/`POKE`/`MEMCOPY` on their internal GLib-backed representation) — this boundary was already correct and stays as-is; only `ARRAY`/`STRUCT`/`STRUCT ARRAY`/scalars/POD-like types get a raw memory view.
10. **`REDIM` may relocate an array's backing storage; a `VARPTR` taken before `REDIM` is not guaranteed valid after it** (documented `realloc`-like semantics, not a bug to "fix" by adding pointer-tracking machinery — deliberately kept simple).
11. **Codex's proposed unifying abstraction**: a shared `MemoryRef` record (`kind`, `owner`, `baseAddress`, `byteOffset`, `byteLength`, `elementStride`, `writable`, `generation`) that every memory-touching op (`VARPTR`/`PEEK*`/`POKE*`/`MEMCOPY*`/`MEMFILL*`) resolves through via one `ResolveMemoryRef()`, instead of each op re-deriving "is this scalar/array/struct" independently. Agreed as the right END STATE, but Claude 1's stated implementation order is: get each engine's OBSERVABLE behavior correct first (single array backing storage, no width loss, correct stride) via more surgical per-engine fixes, THEN fold the logic into the shared abstraction if it doesn't cost another full pass — reversing that order risks a long half-finished refactor that runs nothing correctly in the meantime.

## Implementation order Claude 1 committed to (smallest/independent first)

(a) MEMCOPY canonical parameter order fix + add the Q (64-bit) family.
(b) Fix x64's PEEK/POKE width collapsing to 64-bit at the MIR runtime-call layer.
(c) **The S-036 core**: give the AST interpreter's arrays one real, contiguous backing buffer; make `VARPTR`/`PEEK*`/`POKE*`/`MEMCOPY*` read/write that same buffer instead of a disconnected VM space.
(d) Same for the canonical-MIR interpreter (`MIRValue elements()`-based array storage today; needs the same single-backing-storage treatment).
(e) Native x64: fix the hardcoded-8-byte `elementStride` bug and make `VARPTR` resolve to the array's real address instead of the `<1MiB` magnitude heuristic.
(f) The new `VIRTUAL <ram>[,<disk>]` statement (parser + semantic + all four engines) plus the matching CLI flag and the memory-mapped-file-backed disk extension.

Each step gets verified with a real compile-and-run (not just a read-through) before moving to the next, per this project's standing "verify by actually running it" rule — see [[feedback_no_placeholders_ever]] and [[feedback_verify_before_destructive_action]].

## Status as of this writing (updated 2026-09-14, same day, after implementation began)

**(a) MEMCOPY dst,src,count order: ✅ done, verified.** Fixed in FOUR separate sites (found a previously-unknown exact duplicate: `mir_lower_stmt_core_split.fbs` and `mir_lower_stmt.fbs` both implement the identical "MEMCOPYB/W/D_STMT" MIR-lowering Case — only the second one turned out to be the one actually reached by `run --interpreter-backend MIR`; fixing only the first produced a silently-wrong result until the duplicate was found and fixed too — a warning that this codebase has other undiscovered copy-paste duplicates). Also fixed: AST interpreter (`exec_stmt_memory_core.fbs`), legacy AST-direct x64 (`x64_codegen_stmt_io_console.fbs`'s `X64EmitMemCopyStmt`). Verified via real compile+run on `run`, `run --interpreter-backend MIR`, and `bld --x64-mode AST`.

**(c) AST interpreter NATIVE scalars: ✅ done, verified — but narrower than the full S-036 scope.** `VARPTR`/`PEEKB/W/D`/`POKEB/W/D`/`MEMCOPYB/W/D`/`MEMFILLB/W/D` in explicit `NATIVE` mode (mode is the first positional argument, e.g. `MEMCOPYD NATIVE, dst, src, n` / `PEEKD(NATIVE, addr)` — NOT a bare prefix before the statement keyword, that gets silently swallowed by the statement parser without being recognized) now read/write the REAL address of the variable's own `ExecValue` field (`@ev.intValue`/`@ev.u64Value`/`@ev.floatValue`, via FreeBASIC's own `@` operator — safe because `ExecState.vars` is a fixed-size `0 To 255` array, so these addresses are stable for the ExecState's lifetime). Verified empirically: `POKED NATIVE` written value is visible through an ordinary `PRINT`; `MEMCOPYD NATIVE` moves a real value between two scalars. Scope: only "native scalar" types (I8..U64, F32/F64, PTR/BOOL) — class/interface/OBJECT/TYPE-aggregate targets are deliberately excluded and keep their old `.addr`/VM-based behavior unchanged (no regression, explicitly out of scope). The unprefixed default mode was deliberately NOT changed to NATIVE (would require magnitude-based mode inference to stay safe for aggregates, which the locked design explicitly forbids) — NATIVE/VIRTUAL stay explicit, opt-in. 33/33 `run_typed_task_tests.ps1` regression suite still green.

**Newly discovered, NOT done, explicitly out of scope this pass:**
- **Array element-to-element pointer arithmetic is still wrong.** `VARPTR(arr)` now gives the array's real element-0 address and NATIVE PEEK/POKE/MEMCOPY on that exact address correctly round-trips with ordinary indexed reads/writes (verified) — but `VARPTR(arr) + 4` (one I32 element forward) does NOT land on `arr(1)`, because `ExecArray.elements(Any) As ExecValue` stores one full (large, generic, ~80+ byte) `ExecValue` struct per element regardless of declared type — the real inter-element stride is `SizeOf(ExecValue)`, not `SizeOf(I32)=4`. Fixing this for real needs `ExecArray` to use a tightly-packed, per-declared-type-width raw buffer instead of an `ExecValue` array — a separate, bigger redesign, not attempted here.
- **Struct/class/TYPE fields likely have the identical "two truths" bug**, independent of arrays: the aggregate-scalar/aggregate-array block in `memory_exec.fbs` (~lines 592-681) hands out a real VM address and zero-fills it ONCE at declare time, never keeping it in sync with later field writes — the same root pattern S-036 was originally reported for. Not investigated/fixed this pass.
- **Native x64 (the default MIR-x64 `bld` backend) PEEK/POKE/MEMCOPY still hard-fail** with "unsupported width" at NASM codegen — confirmed PRE-EXISTING (a bare `POKED VIRTUAL, addr, val` alone already fails, before touching MEMCOPY at all), tied to S-021, NOT caused by this session's dst/src fix, NOT fixed this pass (this is locked-design step (b)).
- Steps (d) canonical-MIR array/struct single-backing-storage, (e) native x64 elementStride/VARPTR-via-`__uxb_mem_resolve`, and (f) the new `VIRTUAL <ram>[,<disk>]` statement + CLI flag + disk-backed extension: **not started**.

**Same-day follow-up (2026-09-14, per "start with the recommended one, fix every logical bug found along the way"):**

**Array element-to-element pointer arithmetic: ✅ fixed, verified.** `ExecArray` gained a real, tightly-packed `rawData(Any) As UByte` buffer for arrays whose element type is a native-scalar type; `ExecArrayResizeVar`/`ExecGetArrayElement`/`ExecSetArrayElement`/array-VARPTR all switched to it for that case (REDIM PRESERVE correctly migrates old raw bytes too). `VARPTR(arr) + 4` now correctly reaches `arr(1)` for an I32 array — verified for I32/F64, negative lower bounds, multi-dim, FOR EACH, and REDIM PRESERVE; identical, correct results across AST/canonical-MIR/native-x64 (only the AST interpreter's storage changed; the other two engines were untouched and unaffected). Struct/class fields turned out NOT to have the suspected "two truths" bug on investigation — `ExecReadFieldValue`/`ExecWriteFieldValue` already consistently read AND write through `VMemPeek*/VMemPoke*` (g_vmem) on both sides — no fix needed there.

**CRITICAL SECURITY BUG found and fixed same day: lifting NATIVE's old blanket rejection opened a segfault path.** `VARPTR` on a class/interface/OBJECT/TYPE-aggregate target still returns the OLD, fake, small g_vmem-bookkeeping number (deliberately, since those targets are out of scope for the real-address fix) — but once NATIVE PEEK/POKE/MEMCOPY/MEMFILL became real raw-pointer operations, feeding that stale value to e.g. `PEEKD(NATIVE, VARPTR(structVar))` dereferenced unmapped memory and **crashed the whole interpreter process** (confirmed: "segmentation violation" signal, reproduced then fixed). Fixed by validating every NATIVE address through Win32 `IsBadReadPtr`/`IsBadWritePtr` (`ExecNativeAddrReadable`/`ExecNativeAddrWritable` in `exec_state_value_utils.fbs`) before any dereference — an invalid address now fails closed with a normal uXBasic-level error (matching `VMemPeek*`'s own -1/0 convention) instead of crashing. **Anyone touching NATIVE/VIRTUAL memory code in this project must keep this validation** — a stale/fake address reaching a raw dereference is a live risk any time a target type doesn't yet have real backing.

33/33 regression suite still green after both changes.

**Continued same day under a new tracking number (S-049, ai_koordinasyon/SORUN_TAKIP.md), per the user's "fix everything in order, give it a new number, let everyone know":**

- **Native x64 "unsupported width" (S-021) for PEEK/POKE/MEMCOPY/MEMFILL: ✅ fixed.** Root cause was width being lowered as a temp+MIR_OP_LOAD_CONST instead of a literal (3 files, 6 sites) — the x64 emitter read it with a plain `Val()` which returns 0 for a temp name. Fixing that surfaced two MORE real bugs in sequence: the `__uxb_mem_*_mode` runtime helper labels were never emitted into MIR-x64's own generated .asm at all (only the legacy AST-x64 backend had them — ported verbatim into a new `MIRX64EnsureMemoryModeHelpers`); and my first attempt at that port emitted the helper block inline via `MIRX64Emit` (i.e. into whatever function's body happened to trigger it), which the CPU fell into without a `call`, corrupting the stack via unbalanced `ret` (a real 0xC0000005 crash) — fixed by routing it through a new `cg.memoryModeHelperText` buffer appended only once, after every real function body, in `mir_x64_codegen.fbs`'s final `.asm` assembly.
- **VARPTR unsupported in canonical-MIR and native x64: ✅ fixed.** VARPTR had never been lowered at all (fell through generic CALL_EXPR to an unbound host/library call in both engines). Added a dedicated `MIR_VARPTR` opcode (`mir_lower_expr.fbs`) carrying the identifier as a quoted compile-time literal. Canonical-MIR: handled in `mir_interp_memory.fbs`'s `UXBMIRInterpExecMemory` specifically because that's an `st`-receiving handler group (`MIR_EXPR`'s `UXBMIRInterpExecArith` does NOT receive `st`, so could never have implemented this) — takes the real address of the variable's `UXBInterpValue` field via `@`, with the same documented caveat AST arrays have for REDIM: `st.vars()` is dynamically `ReDim`'d and scope-exit-compacted, so the address is only valid within the variable's own scope. Native x64: turned out `VARPTR` already canonicalizes to `"ADDR_OF"` and a `CODEPTR/LPTR/ADDR_OF` emitter case already existed (`mir_x64_opcode_surface_emitters.fbs`) but had two latent bugs (never stripped the quoted operand; only checked local variables, never globals) — fixed by routing it through the already-correct `MIRX64AddressOfVarToReg`.
- **Canonical-MIR's NATIVE memory family had the exact same blanket rejection AST had before its own fix**: `runtime_memory.fbs`'s `UXBRuntimeMemoryLoadWidth/StoreWidth/CopyMode/FillMode` all did `If modeId = 2 (NATIVE) Then Return 0`. Fixed with the same `IsBadReadPtr`/`IsBadWritePtr`-validated real-pointer approach as AST (the two engines now share one `Declare` for these Win32 functions — FreeBASIC's single combined translation unit rejects declaring the same extern twice, so only `runtime_memory.fbs` keeps the Declare now).
- **Verified**: the same VARPTR+NATIVE MEMCOPYD/POKED/PEEKD test now gives byte-identical correct output across AST, canonical-MIR, and native x64. 33/33 regression suite green throughout; legacy AST-direct x64 (`--x64-mode AST`) and all earlier array tests re-verified unaffected. `bin/uxb.exe` SHA256 after all S-049 work: `AE35103A3EF63A047FE95B57BE85C5F30573D9329E71EC3A864CD4B80FA2983C`.
- **Struct-array (array of TYPE) field access investigated (S-050): the suspected AST "sync" bug was a false alarm** (AST already reads/writes `pts(i).X`-style consistently) — but investigating it surfaced a real, different bug: **canonical-MIR's `pts(i).X` with a runtime-variable index always returned 0** (worked fine with a literal index). Root cause: field access on an indexed-array-of-struct baked the index EXPRESSION'S TEXT (not its runtime value) into a compile-time flat pseudo-variable name like `"PTS(I).X"` — literal indices worked by coincidence (same text on write and read), a variable index could never match. **Fixed** (user approved the "big/correct" option over a narrower patch): added `MIR_ARRAY_FIELD_LOAD`/`MIR_ARRAY_FIELD_STORE` opcodes that route through the array+object heap model already used by plain numeric arrays and CLASS objects (`UXBInterpHeapGetIndex`/`SetIndex`/`GetField`/`SetField`), lazily materializing an element as a heap OBJECT the first time it's touched this way. Found yet another instance of this session's recurring "hidden duplicate file" bug pattern doing this: `ASSIGN_STMT` lowering is duplicated verbatim across `mir_lower_stmt.fbs` and `mir_lower_stmt_core_split.fbs` — both had to be fixed. Only plain `=` assignment was fixed (compound ops like `+=` on an array-of-struct field still use the old, literal-index-only path — unchanged from before, not a new regression). Verified identical to AST across a read+write+FOR-loop test; CLASS fields and plain arrays unaffected; 33/33 regression green. Separately noted, explicitly out of scope: native x64 (default `bld` backend) doesn't support struct arrays AT ALL yet (a compile-time "unsupported array element type" error, not a silent-wrong-result -- an honest, different gap).
- **Still not done as of this line**: the new `VIRTUAL <ram>[,<disk>]` statement + CLI flag + disk-backed extension (not started); native x64 struct-array support (not started, separate feature gap); compound-assignment (`+=` etc.) on array-of-struct fields in canonical-MIR (still literal-index-only).

**Same-day follow-up #2 (2026-09-14, locked-design step (f), AST-interpreter + CLI scope only):**

**The new `VIRTUAL <ramSize>[, <diskSize>]` statement: ✅ done and verified for the AST interpreter (`run`) and its CLI default flag — canonical-MIR and native x64 NOT started (deliberately: native x64 files are Codex's active S-050 CLAIM this same day; canonical-MIR's own `runtime_memory.fbs` still uses a fixed `(0 To 1048575)` static array, untouched).**
- **Parser**: new `ASTK_VIRTUAL_STMT` node kind, `STMT_HANDLER_VIRTUAL` dispatch entry, `ParseVirtualStmt` (`parser_stmt_basic.fbs`) — accepts `VIRTUAL <ram>[, <disk>]`, each operand a bare NUMBER token (optionally K/M/G/T-suffixed, e.g. `2M`). Deliberately did NOT touch the shared lexer/expression pipeline to make suffixed literals "just work" everywhere — the raw token lexeme is stored verbatim on the AST node, and K/M/G/T→bytes scaling (1024-based) happens only at statement-execution time, in a new `ExecParseByteSizeLiteral` (`exec_stmt_memory_core.fbs`).
- **`memory_vm.fbs` rewritten from a RAM-only sandbox into RAM+disk**: `[0, ramBytes)` is the existing RAM `UByte` array; `[ramBytes, ramBytes+diskBytes)` is a NEW disk-backed extension via a real Windows memory-mapped temp file (`CreateFileA` + `CreateFileMappingA` + `MapViewOfFile`, opened with `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_TEMPORARY | FILE_FLAG_DELETE_ON_CLOSE` so the OS deletes it automatically once every handle closes — no hand-rolled swap system, exactly as the locked design specified). Every `VMemPeek*/Poke*/Copy*/Fill*` now goes through one indirection, `VMemByteAt(addr) As UByte Ptr`, that resolves to either the RAM array or the mapped view. `VMemInit` changed from a parameterless `Sub` to a `Function VMemInit(ramBytes, diskBytes, ByRef errText, ...) As Integer` returning success/failure (confirmed via an isolated scratch test that FreeBASIC does allow a default on a `ByRef String` parameter). Re-issuing `VMemInit`/`VIRTUAL` releases the old mapping/temp file first and re-inits everything from zero — matches "REDIM without PRESERVE" semantics exactly as locked, deliberately not preserving old contents.
- **CLI flag `--virtual=<ram>[,<disk>]`**: added to the CLI registry (`cli_registry_adim41.fbs`, option count 171→172). Wiring it to `VMemInit` needed a small workaround: `GetArgValue` (declared in `main_cli_runtime_helpers.fbs`) is textually `#include`'d AFTER `memory_exec.fbs` in the build's single combined translation unit, so it can't be called directly from `ExecRunMemoryProgram`. Fixed with a global, `gUxbCliVirtualArg As String` (declared early, in `memory_exec.fbs`, before it's needed), set once in `main_program_entry.fbs` right after CLI parsing becomes available, and read by `ExecRunMemoryProgram` before running any program statement — the in-program `VIRTUAL` statement can still destructively override this CLI-set default at runtime, exactly as designed.
- **A real language-behavior gotcha hit while testing, NOT a bug in this feature**: in this dialect, suffixless `POKE`/`PEEK` default to a 4-byte (dword) operation — `PEEK`/`PEEKD` literally share one code path (`Case "PEEK", "PEEKD"` in `exec_eval_builtin_categories.fbs`). An early test wrote a dword at the RAM region's very last byte address and got a correct "out of range" rejection that briefly looked like a VIRTUAL bug; it wasn't — byte-level ops need `POKEB`/`PEEKB` explicitly. Worth remembering before assuming any future off-by-N report near a VIRTUAL boundary is this feature's fault.
- **Verified by real compile+run**: RAM-only (`VIRTUAL 2M`) byte and dword poke/peek plus `MEMCOPYB`, all correct. RAM+disk (`VIRTUAL 1M, 4M`): both regions independently read/write correctly, including the disk region's very first and very last byte. Writing one byte past the total (RAM+disk) size fails with a clean `exec:` error, not a crash. Re-issuing `VIRTUAL` mid-program correctly discards all prior RAM+disk contents. `--virtual=1M,4M` sets the CLI default correctly, and an in-program `VIRTUAL 512K` correctly and destructively overrides it (the old disk address becomes out-of-range afterward, as expected). 33/33 regression suite green both with and without `--virtual=`. Full evidence: `ai_koordinasyon/SORUN_TAKIP.md` S-049 item 3.

**Same-day follow-up #3 (2026-09-15): VIRTUAL statement is now DONE across all 4 engines.** Codex wired canonical-MIR (`MIR_VIRTUAL_INIT` opcode, `mir_interp_memory.fbs` reuses the AST's own `VMemInit`/`memory_vm.fbs` directly — `runtime_memory.fbs`'s old fixed `gUXBRuntimeVirtualMemory` array is now genuinely dead) and native x64 (`__uxb_mem_virtual_init` in `mir_x64_context.fbs`, real `CreateFileMappingA`/`MapViewOfFile` for dynamic RAM+disk) overnight. Claude 1 found and fixed 3 real bugs surfaced by this new code while verifying it: (1) **S-057** — out-of-range VIRTUAL access silently returned `0` on native x64 (and, a twin bug, `-1` unchecked on AST's PEEK-family expression forms) instead of a real error; fixed via a checked-call wrapper (`MIRX64EmitMemoryModeCallChecked`) that clears/checks the sticky `__uxb_mem_error` flag around every `__uxb_mem_*_mode` call, mirroring the pattern S-019's native collection ABI already established. (2) A genuine SIGFPE crash (divide-by-zero) in both `UXBMIRInterpParseVirtualBytes` and its byte-for-byte duplicate `MIRX64VirtualSizeLiteral` — Codex's new overflow check used `If n<>0 And mult > ... \ n`, and FreeBASIC's `And` does not short-circuit, so the division ran even when n=0 (the default disk-size text when `VIRTUAL <ram>` is given with no disk argument). Fixed by nesting the `n<>0` check. (3) **S-063** — calling `VIRTUAL` a second time in the same program (the REDIM-without-PRESERVE re-init path) crashed native x64 with a real `0xC0000005`: `__uxb_mem_virtual_init`'s prologue never restored 16-byte stack alignment after its two `push` instructions (function entry is 8-mod-16 per the x64 ABI's own call convention; two pushes, an even count, don't change that), so every WinAPI call inside it was 8 bytes misaligned — `CreateFileMappingA`/`MapViewOfFile` happened not to fault on it, `UnmapViewOfFile`/`CloseHandle` (only reached on a second+ VIRTUAL call, releasing the old mapping) reliably did. Fixed with an extra `sub rsp,8` at entry and matching `add rsp,8` before both returns. **Verified**: a full write+read+reinit+read scenario now gives byte-identical `111,222,111,0` across AST/canonical-MIR/native-x64; 33/33 regression green throughout. Remaining, separately-tracked, non-blocking findings from this same investigation: S-058 (AST's NATIVE memory addresses are 32-bit `UInteger` while canonical-MIR uses 64-bit `ULongInt`), S-059 (NATIVE `POKES`/`PEEKS` accepted/rejected inconsistently across the 3 native-capable backends), S-061 (a negative-valued DWORD PEEK prints as unsigned `4294967295` on AST/canonical-MIR but signed `-1` on native x64 — a display/CInt inconsistency, not a memory-safety bug), S-062 (the legacy, non-default `--x64-mode AST` backend's own mode-blind PEEK/POKE resolver has no bounds check at all above 1MiB and treats the raw address as a native pointer — a different, deeper issue in a different, non-default backend, deliberately left alone this turn). Full detail: `ai_koordinasyon/SORUN_TAKIP.md` S-057/S-063, and the new cross-cutting plan `docs/UXB_ACIK_ISLER_TASARIM_VE_UYGULAMA_PLANI_20260915_TR.md`.

Update this section further with ✅/dates/hashes as each remaining step (S-033/034/035/055/056, S-058/059/061/062) lands, the same way [[uxb-fix-plan-decisions-2026-09]] tracks S-019/S-032/S-046/S-047.
